key_insight: Coercivity-aware, uncertainty-informed machine learning can efficiently narrow rare-earth-free soft-magnetic alloy candidates, with Fe-Co-rich compositions emerging as the most promising.
engineering_relevance: The workflow helps materials engineers screen alloy chemistries for high Curie temperature and low coercivity while accounting for the fact that unseen-composition performance is harder than random-split estimates.
method: Compiled magnetic-material data with composition-grouped train/test splits to prevent identical compositions from leaking across partitions
Compared elemental-fraction features with composition-weighted elemental descriptors for predicting Curie temperature and coercivity
Added residual-based prediction intervals and distance-to-training filters to screen Fe-Co-Ni-Mn-Al-Si candidates
evidence_signal: Composition-grouped evaluation produced lower accuracy than random partitioning, and weighted elemental descriptors improved Curie-temperature prediction but did not improve coercivity prediction.
watch_item: Coercivity is strongly affected by processing and microstructure, so composition-only models may miss key real-world effects and require experimental validation.
paper_title: Coercivity-Aware Machine Learning Discovery of Rare-Earth-Free Soft Magnetic Alloys with First-Principles Magnetic Benchmarks
